\section[śa]{\ml{ശ} (śa) — the letter that opens \ml{ശരി}}

\label{lesson:ML-W113-sha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ml{ഠ} and \ml{ഫ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ml{ശരി}} (\emph{śari}), \textquotedblleft{}okay\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ml{ശ}}
\textbf{\ml{ശ}} — \emph{śa}, the sound \emph{sh}.

It opens \textbf{\ml{ശരി}} (\emph{śari}), \textquotedblleft{}okay\textquotedblright{}, one of the first words in this book.

\subsection*{Writing: \ml{ശ}}
Put your pen on \ml{ശ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ml{ശരി}} and point at \ml{ശ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ml{ശ} three times, saying \emph{ś} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ml{ഫ}, then \ml{ശ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ml{ശരി}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ml{ശ}? (\textbf{śa}, \emph{ś}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ml{ശരി}}, \emph{śari}, \textquotedblleft{}okay\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}

Now say \textbf{\ml{നിങ്ങൾ}} (\emph{niṅṅaḷ}), \textquotedblleft{}you (respectful)\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ml{ങ}}
\textbf{\ml{ങ}} — \emph{ṅa}, the nasal made where \emph{k} is made.

It is inside \textbf{\ml{നിങ്ങൾ}} (\emph{niṅṅaḷ}), the respectful \textquotedblleft{}you\textquotedblright{}, where it is written \textbf{twice}, one on top of the other, for the long \emph{ṅṅ}.

Put your pen on \ml{ങ} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ml{നിങ്ങൾ}} and point at \ml{ങ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ml{ങ} three times, saying \emph{ṅ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ml{ശ}, then \ml{ങ}, from memory

\section[ḷa]{\ml{ള} (ḷa) — the letter inside \ml{നാളെ}}

\label{lesson:ML-W113-lla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ml{ശ} and \ml{ങ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ml{നാളെ}} (\emph{nāḷe}), \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ml{ള}}
\textbf{\ml{ള}} — \emph{ḷa}, an \emph{l} made with the tongue curled back.

It is inside \textbf{\ml{നാളെ}} (\emph{nāḷe}), \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\ml{നാളെ} \ml{കാണാം}}, \textquotedblleft{}see you tomorrow\textquotedblright{}. The dot under the romanization (\emph{ḷ}) is what marks the curled tongue.

\subsection*{Writing: \ml{ള}}
Put your pen on \ml{ള} and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

\begin{quote}
This book does not yet tell you \textbf{where to start this letter or which way to travel}. It is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ml{നാളെ}} and point at \ml{ള} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ml{ള} three times, saying \emph{ḷ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ml{ങ}, then \ml{ള}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ml{നാളെ}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ml{ള}? (\textbf{ḷa}, \emph{ḷ}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ml{നാളെ}}, \emph{nāḷe}, \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
